We examine perceived credibility, belief, and judgment accuracy. Results show that influencer attribution lowers perceived credibility and reduces confidence in accurate political information compared with national news, although these differences vary by ideological orientation. Followers initially report greater belief in false political claims attributed to influencers than recognizers, but this difference weakens substantially after accounting for observed differences between the groups. These findings suggest that influencers’ impact as political information sources depends on both audience characteristics and selection into influencer audiences, underscoring the distinction between audience reach and epistemic authority in hybrid media systems.
